title: Evaluating the Feasibility, Acceptability, and Preliminary Efficacy of Virtually Delivered Dialectical Behaviour Therapy Skills Groups Among Emerging Adults in India
abstract: ABSTRACT Research from high‐income countries has demonstrated the effectiveness of Dialectical Behavioural Therapy (DBT) in reducing a range of psychiatric symptomatology, with limited research on efficacy in low‐and middle‐income countries. The purpose of this study was to examine acceptability, feasibility, and preliminary efficacy of an eight‐week group DBT Skills Training (DBT‐ST) delivered via synchronous video teleconferencing by student therapists in India. Individuals who indicated an interest in participating in a virtual skills program were invited to participate in the study. Those who provided consent were randomized into a virtual DBT‐ST group ( n = 43) or a waitlist comparison group ( n = 41). Participants completed self‐report measures of emotion dysregulation, coping, anxiety, and depression at baseline, after 4 weeks of virtual DBT‐ST groups, and after 8 weeks of virtual DBT‐ST groups. Participants in the virtual DBT‐ST group also responded to open‐ended questions regarding acceptability and feasibility and rated treatment acceptance. Feasibility was demonstrated by the retention of 71.8% of participants. DBT‐ST was rated as acceptable. Efficacy was partially supported: Participants in the DBT‐ST group reported lower depressive symptoms than the comparison group at post‐assessment. There were no significant differences in emotion dysregulation, dysfunctional coping, or anxiety.
